items.title: As they return to the UK, Harry and Meghan search for a brand that sticks
items.summary: They will not be working royals when they come back. So what could they be doing instead?
items.content:
In late July, the Duchess of Sussex's lifestyle range, called As ever, launched a "rich, vibrant" blackberry spread alongside a softly lit video of her picking the fruit.

A month later, Meghan and her husband Prince Harry are returning to live in the UK just as blackberry season ends. Perhaps we can expect another video soon, shot on these shores.

Or perhaps not, because experts say the Harry and Meghan brand is at a crossroads.

After the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's acrimonious exit from the Royal Family in 2020, the projects marking their fresh start in California - from streaming to signature scents - have mostly failed to find large audiences, and experts say it's unclear where the couple goes from here.

Their return to the UK has surprised many and we don't know their reasons for the switch, but what's clear is that they will not be working royals when they return. So what could they be doing instead?

Meghan in talks for role in Netflix series The Gentlemen, BBC understands

Prince Harry and six others face privacy case legal bill of up to £34.5m

Andrew Stephen, the L'Oréal professor of marketing at the University of Oxford's Saïd Business School, says that after they moved to the US the Sussexes "attracted enormous attention and were initially very good at monetising it. But I don't think they have been as successful at converting that initial success into an enduring brand."

Now, he says, they have a "fragmented portfolio spanning social impact, entertainment and lifestyle, which has made it difficult to know exactly what their brand stands for".

After splitting with the Royal Family, the Sussexes said they would work to become financially independent. They began life as civilians with interviews about their relationship with the royals before pivoting to new fields of interest, including media production and lifestyle, which now appears to be Meghan's focus.

The couple's aim, according to the mission statement of their Archewell Productions company, is to highlight "our common humanity and celebrate community". They have continued to promote the Invictus Games, the sporting event for injured service men and women that Prince Harry founded, and launched charitable projects around the world through Archewell Philanthropies.

They are widely reported to have earned $100m (£73m) from a deal with Netflix in 2020. An agreement in the same year with Spotify to produce podcasts was reported to be worth $25m (£18m).

By most metrics, it would be hard to call either of those projects a success. The five years of the Netflix deal yielded five shows, including the six-part series Harry & Meghan and two series of the lifestyle show With Love, Meghan, drawing underwhelming streaming numbers . The deal was replaced last year by an arrangement giving Netflix a first look at any pitches from the couple. Only one new Archewell production has been announced so far this year.

Meanwhile, in 2023, a joint statement from Archewell Productions and Spotify said they had "mutually agreed to part ways" . Spotify confirmed it was not renewing Meghan's 12-episode podcast Archetypes for a second series.

After years of global headlines and their high-profile move to California, Prince Harry and Meghan are preparing for a return to the UK.

One challenge facing the Sussexes on their return is that they are once more associated with the Royal Family from which they have tried to stay separate, says Stephen.

"It could make them feel more culturally relevant by bringing them closer to the centre of British royal life," he says, "but it would also reinforce how dependent their distinctiveness remains on royalty, potentially undermining their attempt to build a more independent, American-style celebrity, media and lifestyle brand."

The fact the Sussexes have switched between projects brings risks to their brand, says Susan Fournier, a branding expert and former professor at Harvard Business School and Boston University. She says the couple went from royal insiders, giving a glimpse into a secret world, to royal critics, then from media producers to, in Meghan's case, a lifestyle influencer.

"Every time a brand does a 180 like that, you can't go back," Fournier tells the BBC. The most successful brands, she says, are consistent in the image that they present - and a return to the UK risks looking like another U-turn.

A solution, Stephen says, would be for them to focus on "a coherent portfolio of focused businesses and credible causes".

The couple have other income sources , from inheritance to the sales of Harry's memoir Spare, which was the fastest-selling non-fiction book in the UK since records began in 1998. A return to acting for Meghan even appears possible.

The BBC has learned she is in talks about a role in Netflix series The Gentlemen , a comedy series created by Guy Ritchie about a duke who becomes a drug baron. No details have yet been revealed, but this would be Meghan's first significant acting role since her marriage to Prince Harry.

Since 2024, Meghan's professional focus has been on her lifestyle range, As ever, which was initially supported by Netflix before that partnership ended in March . As ever sells jams, teas, candles and other products "crafted to elevate your everyday and inspire moments of joy", and there is no indication that it will end when she moves across the Atlantic.

One potential opportunity is their mooted move to the A-list haven of the Cotswolds, where they are believed to have spent time earlier this summer.

Laura Stoloff, an American stylist and creative director who lives in London and the Cotswolds with her British husband Harry, sees "a natural connection" between Meghan's lifestyle brand and Cotswolds life.

"I actually think it could make her brand more distinctive," Stoloff tells the BBC. "There is still a lot of fascination with English country life, particularly in America, and she has the ability to bring that to a very large, global audience."

Stephen has a warning, though: "A return to the UK could be a useful brand reset, but a postcode does not reposition a brand. Behaviour does."

Harry and Meghan's return to UK reignites questions over security

items.title: Drugs at their fingertips, intense pressure: Why child stars fall into addiction
items.summary: Experts told the BBC the pressures of childhood stardom can put actors at an unusually higher risk of substance abuse issues.
items.content:
Hayden Panettiere was 16 when drugs first arrived in her life in Hollywood.

Ahead of a red carpet event for the hit series Heroes, she has said someone on her team handed her a pill to help amp up her energy. The hit sci-fi NBC series had catapulted the teen into a household name - and that brought with it intense pressure and exhaustion she says felt overwhelming.

"Within minutes, a wave of energy washed over me, like I'd just woken up from the most refreshing night's sleep of my life," Panettiere wrote about that pill in her memoir, which was released just months before her death.

She called it "the gateway drug that ushered me toward the good of pharmaceuticals and the downfall of addiction".

The star's sudden death at the age of 36 has placed a renewed focus on her struggles with mental health and substance abuse, and re-ignited a discussion about the pressures of Hollywood on child stars.

The coroner's office in Greenville, South Carolina said crews treated a woman in "cardiac arrest" and her autopsy showed "no signs of trauma".

No cause of death has been released, though additional tests are yet to be completed.

Audio from police dispatchers and crews who responded to the address said they were responding to a "cardiac arrest" and detailed their efforts to resuscitate the woman after a possible "overdose". Panettiere's ex boyfriend, Brian Hickerson - who has admitted to abusing her - and his brother Zack, were with Panettiere when emergency services came, according to a police report.

There is no suggestion of wrongdoing on their part, according to police.

It is not known if drugs or alcohol played a factor in her death, but the US Drug Enforcement Agency is joining an investigation into her death, according to US media reports.

Panettiere is one of many actors who has openly struggled with addiction after exposure to fame at an early age, which addiction experts told the BBC can put people at risk for mental health and substance abuse issues.

It can sometimes seem to the rest of the world that child actors have "everything" at their fingertips - like fame and money, said Lucas Trautman, the medical director of Oxford Treatment Center, an addiction treatment centre in Mississippi.

"But it's important to remember that they were also exposed during a developmental time to many adult aspects of life that the rest of us weren't - including traumatic experiences - and so that gives them unique risk factors for addiction," Trautman said.

Panettiere's death comes after she published a memoir where she discussed at length her issues with addiction, her postpartum depression and the loss of her 28-year-old brother.

Panettiere's decision to publicly share her struggles is worthy of respect, said William Moyers, the vice-president of public affairs for Hazelden Betty Ford, the largest nonprofit addiction treatment provider in the US. But he said the constant public scrutiny she faced may not have allowed her room to address her mental health in private.

"Her entire life from the beginning was centred in the intense public spotlight, and this didn't give Hayden much in the way of a respite," said Moyers, who has been in recovery from an addiction since 1989.

Tributes to actress Hayden Panettiere as coroner finds 'no signs of trauma'

Hayden Panettiere: A life of struggles alongside screen success

In pictures: Hayden Panettiere's life and career, from child actor to Scream star

Trautman - who has treated child stars - said they often have "adult access" to drugs and alcohol without adult protection.

"We aren't equipped at a young age to be able to say no to it, to manage it, to correctly stay away from it altogether," he said.

Other child stars have talked about being exposed to drugs at an early age, including Drew Barrymore, who went to rehab at 12, and Demi Lovato, a Disney Channel star.

"I got into a car accident and they prescribed me opiates. My mum didn't think she would have to lock up the opiates from her 13-year-old daughter, but I was already drinking at that point," the singer told podcast Call Her Daddy in 2022.

Actress Michelle Rodriguez, who once hosted the World Music Awards with Panettiere, said this week that the number of child actors who had passed away at a young age was strange.

"I just can't stand how many young people are leaving us lately. It's disheartening, and it's making me think, 'What's going on?' It's not normal," she told Variety.

Panettiere's death comes just a year after the death of Michelle Trachtenberg and months after Daveigh Chase, two child stars who both struggled with drugs and alcohol.

In an essay she wrote after Panettiere's death, former Disney star Christy Carlson Romano compared early fame to a traumatic brain disease.

"[W]e have almost no language for what happens when stress, scrutiny, rejection, adult pressure, and the collapse of privacy become the architecture of a childhood," she wrote.

And when a child actor's career changes or comes to an end, they are left without the dopamine of fame and money that came with their identity as an actor, cautioned Trautman.

"At the same time many of them self medicated... so their brain is still reliant on that, and it's really really hard to stop using," he said.

Many child stars also have professional relationships with their parents, which can blur boundaries and leave them vulnerable, Trautman said.

In her book and in the media, Panettiere has discussed the pressure her mother placed on her to excel as an actress from an early age. She appeared in her first commercial when she was just 11-months-old.

"You always want to think the best of your parents and see them in the brightest light," the actress told the New York Times in May. "But there were a lot of things done with an approach that was not about my mental health or what was emotionally or mentally safe for me to do."

Substance abuse also puts people at risk for a host of medical conditions, including heart disease and liver and other organ damage.

Panettiere's brother, Jansen, died aged 28 from a heart condition, and Panettiere revealed in her book that her brother was using heroin and cocaine leading up to his death.

But after he died, the actress told People Magazine in 2024 she was committed to staying sober, telling the outlet her addiction was "in the rear view mirror".

She said in her book that at one point a doctor told her that if she did not stop drinking, she would be "dead within five years".

For Moyers and other substance abuse experts, addiction is a chronic illness, meaning that relapses still happen even while treatment saves lives.

"Living in recovery means doing the best we can, but doing it imperfectly," he said.

items.title: TikTok to pay $400m to US in one of largest child privacy settlements
items.summary: The deal stems from a 2024 lawsuit alleging TikTok and its parent company ByteDance collected "vast amounts of data" on millions of users under the age of 13.
items.content:
TikTok has agreed to pay $400m (£293m) to the US to end a lawsuit alleging its platform violated children‘s privacy, marking one of the largest ever settlements over the issue.

The deal stems from a 2024 suit by the Department of Justice under former President Joe Biden alleging TikTok and its parent company ByteDance collected "vast amounts of data" on millions of users under the age of 13.

Doing so was against the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA), a federal law enacted in 2000. It is the same law that dozens of US states are now suing Meta over .

"Children and parents are better protected today than they were when this case began," assistant Attorney General Brett Shumate said.

Other companies to have paid penalties to the US government for COPPA violations include Google's YouTube, which in 2019 paid $170m, and Epic Games, which in 2022 paid $275m.

Meta is also now facing penalties that could exceed hundreds of billions of dollars stemming from COPPA violations alleged by attorneys general of 29 US states. A jury trial in the lawsuit started this week , with the Instagram and Facebook owner accused of targeting child users and profiting from them.

While the TikTok lawsuit predates last year's split of TikTok's US business and operations from its original base of China, the settlement only involves TikTok's operations in China.

ByteDance, which is a privately held company, was most recently valued by investors at $550bn , external .

Under the terms of the deal, TikTok and ByteDance will immediately pay the DOJ $300m. It will pay another $100m when the government vacates a 2019 consent decree , external with the Federal Trade Commission.

As part of the agreement, the predecessor to ByteDance, Musical.ly, was required to pay a $5.7m fine for COPPA violations and ensure it sought parental consent for any user aged under 13.

The justice department did not detail on Friday any action against TikTok beyond the fine. But the department noted that since it sued the platform, TikTok has "undergone significant changes," including to its ownership, privacy practices and platform controls for young users.

When the lawsuit was filed, attorneys for the US said there were more than 170 million teenagers using TikTok and that the app was "directed to children." Yet, it did not effectively gauge the age of users or get parental consent for use from those underage.

In 2024, former President Biden pushed for TikTok to be either banned, or have the company divest its US operations. President Donald Trump went on to support divestment of the app, which occurred last year.

Its US operations are now 81% owned by a consortium of investors, while Bytedance maintains a 19% stake.

A representative of TikTok did not respond to the BBC for comment.

US states call for big changes to Instagram and Facebook as Meta child privacy trial begins

Meta hooked children on Facebook and Instagram, US court hears

Is the US-China TikTok deal done? Here's what you need to know

items.title: These bookshops let Chinese readers question their country - now the doors are closing
items.summary: For some mainlanders, Hong Kong's independent bookstores are a window into a different, freer world.
items.content:
When Chen Zhu heads to Hong Kong from mainland China every month, there's one place she always goes: Hunter Bookstore.

Founded four years ago by a former councillor, the independent bookshop has earned a reputation for stocking what authorities would consider sensitive books - from accounts of Hong Kong's pro-democracy campaigners, to famous allegories on authoritarianism, such as George Orwell's Animal Farm or Hajime Isayama's Manga series Attack on Titan.

It's a short journey from Zhu's home in Guangzhou on China's southern coast to the crowded street in Hong Kong's Sham Shui Po district, where Hunter is sandwiched between fabric sellers, garages and trendy cafes.

But, for the 23-year-old, it is also a passage into a different, freer world - where she can find answers to forbidden questions.

When she learned the bookshop had been raided by police in late June, Zhu broke into tears: "I was devastated."

Hong Kong saw a boom in independent bookshops after huge pro-democracy protests rocked the city in 2019. But it has been increasingly difficult for them to survive as China's control over the city has grown.

While Beijing defends its far-reaching National Security Law (NSL) as essential for stability, many Hong Kongers and rights groups argue it has crushed free speech. Thousands of locals, including activists and former lawmakers, have left in recent years, as tough new security laws have led to a slew of arrests and convictions.

When police searched Hunter Bookstore on 24 June, they accused owner Letitia Wong, 33, and a 32-year-old man, of violating those laws and arrested them for sedition and money laundering. They deny the charges and have since been released on bail.

In March, they arrested the owner of Book Punch, along with three employees on the same charges, and reportedly seized copies of a biography on Jimmy Lai, the jailed democracy campaigner.

On 15 July, when the annual Hong Kong Book Fair opened, national security police searched two more independent bookshops, Greenfield Bookstore and Have a Nice Stay, arresting five people for sedition. They, too, have been released on bail.

At the end of the month Greenfield posted on social media, saying: "Our store will be closing after our lease expires. Thank you for walking with us, through wind and rain, for 50 years since our opening." It was the third independent bookshop to shut within a month.

These bookshops have long had a loyal following not just in Hong Kong, but also among many mainland Chinese readers. Some like Zhu travel to the city in search of a single book.

For 19-year-old Li from Shanghai, who didn't give her first name, these are places where she "can see so many possibilities, and where existing ideas can be challenged". Others treasure them as spaces that offer a sense of freedom and community they feel is missing on the mainland.

Now they fear China is eroding that spirit in Hong Kong too.

When Zhu began university in 2021, she became increasingly curious about lesser-discussed chapters of Chinese history - such as the 1989 Tiananmen Square massacre, a taboo topic that has been scrubbed off the country's tightly controlled internet.

The massive student-led protests ended in a bloody army crackdown whose toll is still contested. Beijing said at the time that 200 civilians died, but according to de-classified UK diplomatic cables, at least 10,000 people were killed.

Zhu sought out films which touch on the era-defining event, but neither epic romance Summer Palace nor the secretly filmed gay drama Lan Yu could satisfy her curiosity.

She became set on tracking down The Unburned Book by Taiwanese poet Yang Du, a bittersweet reflection on protesters who later went into exile.

In 2023, as soon as the China-Hong Kong border reopened after the pandemic she made her way to Hong Kong to find it.

This was when the city's independent bookshops were taking off. People were sharing walking routes online, complete with neighbourhood guides and curated recommendations.

In bustling Mong Kok there was Luck Win, known for its generous discounts, and Greenfield, with its packed floor-to-ceiling shelves. A short walk away were the cosy Have a Nice Stay, founded by former journalists, which held popular late-night reading sessions, and Elmbook, whose cramped but beloved shelves made regulars feel like they were on a treasure hunt.

Then there was Book Punch on trendy Tai Nan Street, with a collection as defiant as its motto, "one punch to wake the reader", and the food lovers' favourite, Word by Word in historic Wan Chai, and, of course, Hunter, with a sofa outside where passers-by can take a break.

That's where Zhu found The Unburned Book. She had tried - and failed - in other stores, so she was surprised when she finally spotted it.

Hong Kong, once a refuge for those fleeing China post 1989, commemorated the killings every year with a vigil. They gradually disappeared as the new laws targeted political gatherings.

Still, when Chris, 20, whose name we have changed, travelled to Hong Kong in early June, he found that one bookstore was displaying relevant books, white candles and rolls of masking tape printed with the Roman numerals "VI-IV" - 6-4, a coded way of representing the 4 June anniversary.

These young people may not be from Hong Kong, but they describe feeling a deep sense of belonging in these bookshops: politically vibrant spaces that engage with the history their governments would rather they forget.

Li visited Hong Kong during the Lunar New Year earlier this year, months after a massive apartment blaze in the north-eastern Tai Po district claimed 168 lives.

At Hunter Bookstore, she discovered a wall covered in black sticky notes, where visitors had left messages of encouragement for those affected by the tragedy.

Li says this sense of community is difficult to find in mainland China. She says while they have message boards there too, they wouldn't be focused on solidarity with victims of one particular incident, perhaps because authorities are wary of any outpouring of public sentiment. "People can only express themselves indirectly," Li says.

She was equally struck by another small detail: handwritten notes left by staff alongside the books. Using sticky notes, booksellers had shared reflections on books they had read or highlighted passages they found particularly meaningful. It's not something she had ever seen back home.

Zhu experiences something similar. "We all love books. We all value independent bookshops. That's why we choose to buy books here."

She rarely speaks to strangers while browsing, but she never feels like an outsider. The books and events the shops host give her the feeling she's escaped to somewhere with "at least a little freedom of expression".

"You've left mainland China behind. Of course, you know [this] freedom has its limits. But it's still better than not being able to say anything at all."

She says she finds herself encountering authorities more often in Hong Kong than in mainland China. At one bookshop event, she recalls government officials entering the premises. "They just sat there listening alongside us."

Increasing raids have not only targeted explicitly political shops, according to a bookseller who asked not to be identified because of possible repercussions.

"Luck Win Bookstore and Elmbook have always kept a very low profile," the bookseller says.

"They rarely make public statements or organise events. I genuinely can't think of anything they could have done to offend the government."

In the weeks leading up to this year's book fair, both shops were criticised in Wen Wei Po, a newspaper controlled by Beijing's liaison authorities in Hong Kong.

The paper accused them of selling books promoting "soft resistance". This included The Hong Kong Diaries by the last governor of Hong Kong, Chris Patten, before the city returned to Chinese rule, and 300 Short Essays by late Apple Daily columnist Lee Yee. The newspaper was shuttered and several senior staff, including its owner Jimmy Lai, were jailed for violating the new security laws.

"The authorities don't want people to know exactly where the boundaries are," says Tong Kin-long of University College London. "They want people to work out the red lines for themselves, or to censor themselves before crossing them."

Watching these changes unfold in Hong Kong has felt strangely familiar to a man we are calling K, in his 30s from Sichuan.

He remembers a time when mainland China's bookshops were also vibrant spaces for public discussion. Liberal books and magazines would be prominently displayed. Bookshops regularly hosted talks and discussions. But around 2015, he began to notice a gradual tightening.

At first it was books about the country's leaders. But then less obviously sensitive books started disappearing. Public events became less frequent, and the atmosphere changed.

Zhu has a friend who currently runs a bookshop in Guangzhou. She says police occasionally visit the shop to harass the bookseller. During film screenings organised by the bookshop, the electricity has even been cut off.

items.title: Modi spent years building his strong image - why is he making Gen Z reels now?
items.summary: Narendra Modi's new, more casual online persona is drawing attention from young Indians - but also plenty of scepticism.
items.content:
Many among India's Gen Z may not see Narendra Modi as a friend. But the Indian prime minister is trying to talk to them like one.

The 75-year-old leader - who has long cultivated a strongman image through scripted speeches, formal broadcasts and carefully choreographed appearances - has in recent weeks adopted a more casual style on Instagram, the photo and video platform popular with young people.

Modi's timeline, which until a month ago featured carefully curated posts, now also includes more "candid" content, such as a get-ready-with-me reel and several selfie-style addresses to young people, whom he calls "friends".

In one video, he even refers to a phrase popular among Gen Z, saying, " first in my bloodline , external to build a rocket, a chip and a drone" while addressing students at a graduation ceremony in Delhi.

Modi has more than 106 million followers on Instagram, making him one of the most-followed political leaders on the platform.

But the tone of his communication on the platform was never central to his team or the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) social media strategy, despite the party's reputation for acing the digital playbook that helped it win the 2014 elections.

However, things changed after the youth protests in India this year.

Led by the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), the movement spread through memes, livestreams and Instagram reels before evolving into a force strong enough to make a federal minister resign.

The CJP began as a joke, but its ability to turn online attention into street mobilisation and political pressure appeared to catch the BJP off guard.

For more than a decade, the Hindu nationalist party has built one of India's most formidable political forces online using WhatsApp groups, Facebook pages and X accounts to amplify its message, says author and commentator Anurag Minus Verma.

More than 60% of India's population is under 35 and Gen Z (born between 1997 and 2012) is expected to form one of the country's largest voting blocs by the 2029 general election, experts say.

Winning them over means reaching them on platforms such as Instagram, where personal and unfiltered content can resonate more than traditional political messaging.

That shift was evident when Modi's posts first appeared on Instagram. Young users were quick to respond with sarcasm.

Many people mocked his first selfie-video reel , external - in which he broke his silence about the youth protests while they were still ongoing. But what really caught their attention was a long pause after Modi said, "friends".

Versions of it soon trended online, with users adding edits and jokes and mocking the lighting and camera angles in his video.

In the posts that followed, Modi's team appeared to respond to some of that criticism, experimenting with different camera angles, backdrops and lighting.

While some young users appreciated the outreach, many were still sceptical about its timing.

Ginni Malia, 22, "understands" why the BJP wants to connect with people her age, but says "the timing of this sudden increased engagement is what we really need to look at".

The videos appear to adopt Gen Z language and formats, but fail to address concerns that fuelled the protests, she adds.

It is not just Modi's account. BJP social media pages have also started using memes, slang and pop-culture references to reach younger audiences.

Shortly after the protests ended, the BJP posted a reel set in a gym , external . It featured young people and an older trainer arguing that young Indians should stay away from the protests. But many comments and shares called the video "cringe".

Another video posted by the BJP had the 90s sitcom Friends title track playing in the background, with the caption, " PM Modi is there for you , external " - a reference to a show that was a hit with millennials but has little recall value among Gen Z.

Malia says among her peers, these videos are seen as "comic content" rather than taken as political messaging or outreach.

According to reports, the BJP seems to be aware that its attempts to reach younger audiences were not landing as intended.

During the protests, Modi reportedly asked his cabinet ministers to increase their social media engagement and reach out to the youth.

On Wednesday, federal ministers were given a "report card" on their social media performance and told to step up their presence across platforms, the Hindustan Times reported.

Recently, the party also replaced its social media chief Amit Malviya who had held the post since 2015. Some analysts say it could be because of criticism directed at the BJP online during the protests and how they were unable to contain the social media narrative.

The BJP is not alone in trying to connect with younger audiences.

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi - who often posts selfie-style videos and candid pictures on Instagram - also held an Instagram Ask Me Anything after the protests, with playful responses such as "have you seen me and Batman in the same room together?"

However, getting attention on Instagram is one thing and controlling the conversation there is another.

Joyojeet Pal, who teaches the political use of social media at the University of Michigan, says the BJP has long relied on a network of supporters on X and WhatsApp to amplify its messages and shape the narrative - but that does not work on Instagram.

The platform tends to push content that generates more engagement, such as longer watch times, replays, shares and comments.

"It is not too difficult to find a reel which has 10 million views posted from an account that has 200 followers, while some posted by people with a huge base might do only a few thousand," Pal says.

"This is a challenge for the BJP because its strategy was built for a network-centric internet, while today's platforms are far more affect-centric."

Another hurdle for the BJP could be losing control over what happens after a video is posted.

Modi's first reel, which has been viewed more than 400 million times, is a case in point. While it attracted a huge audience, Verma says young people reshared it with sarcastic and mocking edits, giving it a very different tone from what Modi intended. For the BJP, learning to accept that dynamic could be a challenge.

"Instagram is fundamentally a platform built around irony," says Verma. "Serious political messaging, packaged as reels, can still be trolled."

Experts, however, caution against putting too much weight on the BJP's efforts to win over Gen Z. They say the party's electoral success still depends far more on its organisational strength and loyal support base than on how its content performs on Instagram.

"It's important to distinguish between the ability to win an election and to win a social-media narrative," Pal says. "The BJP is absolutely capable of sweeping elections even if every Gen Z person hates it on social media."

For now, the party - like many in India's political space - is learning to operate in unfamiliar territory.

But it would not be surprising if the BJP eventually figures it out it, Pal says.

The party has a history of adapting to new forms of political communication, from being an early adopter of social media for campaigning to embracing newer formats such as podcasts and influencer interviews.

"But it will take time, and the fact that we are seeing this problem now means that they will have to learn a new set of rules," he adds.

items.title: Watch: Taking a 180mph spin round America's birthday Grand Prix racetrack
items.summary: The Freedom 250 Grand Prix is part of the nation’s 250th anniversary celebrations and the first major auto race in the US capital in more than 24 years.
items.content:
The BBC's Helena Humphrey took a test drive ahead of the Freedom 250 Grand Prix, where IndyCar race cars will push speeds of 180mph in Washington DC.

The Freedom 250 Grand Prix is part of a belated celebration of the nation’s 250th anniversary, and the event is expected to attract about 140,000 people on each day of the weekend. The event is the first major auto race in the capital in more than 24 years.

items.title: How Israel is expanding settlements in drive to reshape West Bank
items.summary: There has been a significant expansion of building and road construction on Palestinian land occupied by Israel in recent years.
items.content:
It was during a ceremony at a settlement in the occupied West Bank last September that Israel's prime minister made his intentions clear. "We are going to fulfill our promise that there will be no Palestinian state," said Benjamin Netanyahu. "This place belongs to us."

He was signing an agreement to push ahead with the expansion of a settlement in an area known as E1, just to the east of Jerusalem.

In recent days, the opening up of tenders for the construction of some 1,200 settlement homes on the strategically important land has brought widespread condemnation.

All settlements are illegal under international law and, under global pressure, Israel held off for decades on plans to build in the area.

After the recent announcement, the UN secretary general said they posed an "existential threat" to a future Palestinian state, while a joint statement by the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada said the plans were "unacceptable" and would "drive a wedge through the West Bank", a sentiment echoed by the European Union.

That was welcomed by Mahmoud Abbas, president of the Palestinian Authority, who called for the signatories to take "concrete measures to halt the implementation of the E1 plan".

Along with Gaza and the Golan Heights, the West Bank was captured during the 1967 war against a coalition of Arab states. Israel has controlled it ever since.

As occupied land, international law prohibits Israel from settling it. Despite that, the number of Israelis living there has grown over the years. Israel has built about 160 settlements housing 700,000 Jews since 1967.

There has been a notable increase in the speed of settlement construction since 2022, however, when Netanyahu returned to power at the head of a right-wing, pro-settler coalition, further escalating after the start of the Gaza war, triggered by Hamas's 7 October 2023 attack on Israel.

One example of this is Tzofim, a settlement in the north west of the territory, where BBC Verify analysis of satellite imagery shows the construction of around 185 new buildings since 2022.

The same can be seen around Kochav Hashahar, where the existing settlement has been expanded in multiple directions, with construction of roads, houses and a new settler outpost on surrounding land.

Hundreds of outposts - illegal under Israeli and international law - have been established since the 1990s. Dozens of them have been retrospectively legalised by the government.

Maybe the most contentious is the aforementioned E1 settlement. To understand why, you need to look at maps of its proposed location.

The development would in effect divide the West Bank in two and isolate East Jerusalem from the rest of the territory. Opponents of the project have warned that it would effectively block the establishment of a Palestinian state because it would cut off the north of the West Bank from the south, and prevent the development in the centre of a contiguous Palestinian urban area connecting Ramallah, East Jerusalem and Bethlehem.

Peace Now, an Israeli anti-settlement watchdog that has challenged the plans in court, said: "The government is trying to sign contracts with contractors before the (upcoming October) elections so that it will be much harder for the next government to cancel the construction."

It is not just settlements that have been expanding. Over the last few years, much of the responsibility for the administration of the West Bank has shifted from military control to a civilian authority headed by Bezalel Smotrich, the country's far right finance minister.

This has led to a huge increase in the numbers of roads that cross the West Bank, connecting settlements but bisecting Palestinian towns and villages, something he said "ensures that the settlements will not remain on paper - but will be established on the ground".

In May of this year, the Israeli government announced more than a billion shekels ($360m; £246m) of funding for new road construction in the West Bank, with the intention of "strengthening of their grip on the territory", according to an official press release.

There has also been an escalation of settler violence against Palestinians. Recently, two Palestinian homes were besieged by settlers, with their water and power cut, leading US Ambassador Mike Huckabee, usually a prominent supporter of settlements, to denounce the attack as a "criminal and terrorist act".

All taken together, it has led to fears from Palestinians in the West Bank and supporters of Palestinian statehood that the "facts on the ground" will render it unviable.

According to some senior Israeli ministers, that is the strategy. Speaking in 2024, Smotrich said the construction of E1 would help "establish sovereignty in Judea and Samaria (a name for the occupied West Bank used by Israel), first on the ground and then through legislation… My life's mission is to thwart the establishment of a Palestinian state".

The recent news that the tender has been put out for construction of E1, comes just a couple of months ahead of deeply consequential and tightly contested elections in Israel.

Benjamin Netanyahu and his coalition partners will hope that moves like this appeal to their base and increase their chances of victory. If that is not possible, they may believe that settlement expansion has established new "facts on the ground", ones which cannot be undone.

Additional reporting by Barbara Metzler, BBC Verify. Graphics by Tom Shiel and Mesut Ersoz.

Israel re-establishes closed West Bank settlement, defying growing international protests

items.title: Cosa non funziona in Italia quando una donna denuncia una violenza
items.summary: Dopo il femminicidio di Tania Terrin se lo sta chiedendo anche il governo: la prima cosa da guardare è come vengono usati i centri antiviolenza
items.content:
Dino Keber, l’uomo che il 15 agosto in provincia di Venezia ha ucciso l’ex compagna Tania Terrin e poi si è suicidato, era già stato denunciato da Terrin e da altre donne in passato, ma le istituzioni, in questo caso la questura, si erano attivate nei suoi confronti con una misura di prevenzione che è stata diffusamente giudicata inadeguata (un ammonimento, che spesso ha poche conseguenze concrete).

Restano diversi aspetti da chiarire, ma molti si stanno chiedendo che cosa non abbia funzionato in questa storia. Il ministero della Giustizia sta valutando di inviare ispettori nella procura di Venezia, quella che si era occupata del caso. Chi lavora da tempo sulla violenza maschile contro le donne, però, non ha manifestato lo stesso stupore per come sono andate a finire le cose: da decenni si denuncia che i femminicidi sono in gran parte morti annunciate e che mostrano il fallimento delle risposte istituzionali alla violenza di genere.

Per contrastare la violenza di genere l’Italia è sempre andata nella stessa direzione: reprimere le condotte penalmente rilevanti, approvare norme con nuove fattispecie di reato e introdurre sanzioni sempre più severe. Eppure ha accumulato diverse condanne internazionali per come tratta la violenza di genere: condanne in cui si giudica sufficiente e adeguato il piano normativo, ma in cui si ribadisce che il problema continua a essere il modo in cui le leggi vengono applicate.

Perseguire penalmente la violenza di genere in ogni caso è solo una delle basi su cui si fonda la Convenzione di Istanbul, il primo strumento internazionale giuridicamente vincolante per la prevenzione e il contrasto della violenza contro le donne e della violenza domestica. Le altre tre sono la prevenzione, la protezione (che comprende anche la necessità di informare le vittime dei loro diritti, facendo in modo che sappiano dove e come ottenere aiuto), e l’attuazione di politiche integrate tra vari soggetti, tutte cose che richiedono l’impiego di risorse economiche adeguate.

L’Italia è carente su tutti questi fronti, come segnalato dalle sentenze internazionali ma anche dagli stessi centri antiviolenza, spesso sottofinanziati, insufficienti nel numero e lasciati ai margini.

Manifestazione del movimento femminista Non Una Di Meno davanti al ministero dell’Istruzione e del Merito, 25 novembre 2025 (Valentina Stefanelli/LaPresse)

La giudice di Cassazione Paola Di Nicola Travaglini, esperta in materia e autrice di diversi libri, dice che l’intervento delle istituzioni diventa pienamente efficace «quando è sostenuto dai centri antiviolenza e quando le istituzioni collaborano attivamente con i centri antiviolenza, come stabilito dalle convenzioni internazionali e come accade già nelle migliori prassi giudiziarie». I dati lo confermano.

Da una delle relazioni della Commissione parlamentare d’inchiesta sul femminicidio fatte nella passata legislatura è emerso un dato molto significativo. Analizzando le indagini e le sentenze di quasi 200 casi di femminicidio che si sono verificati nel biennio 2017-2018, è risultato che in soli 5 casi le donne poi uccise si erano rivolte a dei centri antiviolenza. Nella relazione si dice anche che «non sempre le istituzioni che per prime incontrano le donne segnalano i centri antiviolenza come servizi specializzati per le vittime».

Lo studio riferisce che solo in 4 casi la donna era stata informata dei suoi diritti, «con indicazione precisa e chiara anche dei numeri di telefono dei centri antiviolenza cui rivolgersi, mentre in 8 casi era stato consegnato solo uno stampato con citazione di norme di legge». Questo è successo nonostante dal 2009 esista una legge, la numero 38, che obbliga le forze dell’ordine, i presidi sanitari e le istituzioni pubbliche a «fornire alla vittima stessa tutte le informazioni relative ai centri antiviolenza presenti sul territorio».

I centri antiviolenza (che sono gratuiti e sono tenuti alla totale riservatezza e segretezza) «sono i luoghi in cui le donne vengono ascoltate senza essere giudicate, in cui il loro vissuto viene riferito a personale femminile altamente specializzato e preparato all’accoglienza e all’ascolto», spiega Di Nicola Travaglini. Sono i luoghi in cui nessuna viene forzata a parlare o a fare qualche cosa di cui non è convinta: «E sono i luoghi in cui le donne vengono credute», dice la giudice.

Nadia Somma Caiati, presidente del centro antiviolenza Demetra di Lugo, in provincia di Ravenna, dice che nei centri antiviolenza le donne vengono accompagnate nel ripercorrere ciò che hanno vissuto, e che questo sostegno consente loro «di rileggere comportamenti per cui prima non avevano strumenti, e di prenderne dunque coscienza. Permette di capire, solo per fare un esempio, che la parola “gelosia” non è corretta per descrivere quello che hanno passato e che si è trattato piuttosto di “controllo” e di “limitazione della libertà”: di violenza».

I centri antiviolenza sono anche i luoghi, dice Somma Caiati, «in cui si sa molto bene che il cammino di una donna vittima di violenza maschile è fatto di tappe contraddittorie: minimizzazione del pericolo, altalene emotive, determinazione a chiudere la relazione intrecciata con l’incertezza, sensi di colpa, compassione verso il maltrattante. Cose che qui non diventano motivi di giudizi sommari o, peggio, di sottovalutazioni».

Sono poi sempre i centri antiviolenza ad avere le competenze per fare un’adeguata valutazione del rischio in un contesto privo di pregiudizi e stereotipi, e tenendo conto del contesto sociale, familiare ed economico della donna coinvolta: nella relazione della Commissione sul femminicidio si dice che una delle costanti criticità rilevate è che in diversi casi «l’uomo aveva espressamente dichiarato alla polizia giudiziaria di non tollerare e di non poter consentire che la moglie non rispettasse le regole di casa», cosa che anziché essere interpretata come ragione di rischio è stata «addirittura ritenuta normale» e senza alcun nesso con la violenza.

Manifestazione per le vie del quartiere Pigneto a Roma organizzata dopo l’aggressione di una donna, 26 giugno 2026 (Cecilia Fabiano/LaPresse)

Concretamente, le operatrici dei centri antiviolenza possono accompagnare la donna a fare denuncia. Poiché non sempre ci si trova di fronte a forze dell’ordine formate e preparate sul tema, questo garantisce che la denuncia «descriva correttamente tutto ciò che la donna segnala, e che non sia raccolta in modo superficiale omettendo passaggi fondamentali che serviranno alla magistratura per le valutazioni, soprattutto sulle violenze economiche e psicologiche spesso erroneamente non ritenute reato». In questo modo si contribuisce a evitare decisioni inadeguate o archiviazioni.

I centri antiviolenza, oltre a fornire la protezione in una casa rifugio quando il pericolo impone un allontanamento, mettono poi a disposizione delle donne, precisa Di Nicola Travaglini, «avvocate specializzate e competenti», in grado di intervenire quando il sistema rischia di incepparsi e di monitorare tutto ciò che accade dopo le denunce: se le misure cautelari predisposte sono adeguate al caso concreto, per esempio. «I centri antiviolenza sono in grado di fare una valutazione del rischio secondo dati scientifici ed esperienziali e devono entrare in modo strutturato nella filiera della formazione, della prevenzione, della protezione e della fuoriuscita dalla violenza maschile», dice la giudice. Eppure, aggiunge Somma Caiati, sono percepiti come «mero servizio o marginalizzati».

La stessa nuova legge sul femminicidio ne riconosce l’importanza: all’articolo 8 si occupa di rafforzamento degli obblighi formativi in materia di contrasto alla violenza sulle donne, dicendo che deve essere curata da «esperti di comprovata e documentata conoscenza delle materie»: cioè, precisa Di Nicola Travaglini, dai centri antiviolenza.

Spesso il fatto che una donna non denunci viene interpretato come una sua colpa: per le mancate denunce ci sono molti e fondati motivi, ma a parte questo «la magistratura esperta del settore, consapevole dei limiti che tuttora vi sono, suggerisce di denunciare dopo che le donne sono state in un centro antiviolenza e dopo aver trovato un avvocato o un’avvocata specializzati». Che, per questo genere di reati, sono pagati dallo Stato .

«I centri a cui rivolgersi devono essere di comprovata competenza, naturalmente, occuparsi solo e in modo specifico di violenza maschile contro le donne e aderire alla Convenzione di Istanbul», dice Di Nicola Travaglini. È poi importante recarsi, ove possibile, presso le sezioni specializzate di polizia e carabinieri, «dove si possono trovare operatori formati e molto competenti. A quel punto ci sono maggiori probabilità che il percorso, da lì in poi, vada nella giusta direzione».

Dove chiedere aiuto Se hai bisogno di aiuto o sostegno qui c’è l’elenco di tutti i numeri telefonici dei centri antiviolenza della rete Di.Re. È anche possibile chiamare il numero antiviolenza e stalking 1522 , gratuito, attivo 24 ore su 24 con un’accoglienza disponibile in italiano, inglese, francese, spagnolo e arabo. In entrambi i casi si riceveranno indicazioni da persone che hanno l’esperienza e la formazione più completa per occuparsi di questa questione. È anche possibile, di fronte a una situazione di emergenza, chiamare i carabinieri o la polizia al 112.

items.title: Un gruppo di pirati informatici sta pubblicando video di GTA VI per pompare una criptomoneta
items.summary: Il gruppo si fa chiamare Cyberleek e con ogni probabilità è in possesso di una build non definitiva del gioco per PC. Da un paio di giorni pubblica video di gameplay per guadagnare con una criptomoneta. I fondi servirebbero per un misterioso progetto "contro il sistema" ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Da alcuni giorni un gruppo di cybercriminali che si fa chiamare Cyberleek sta pubblicando video di gameplay da quella che appare essere una build non definitiva dell'attesissimo GTA VI. L'ultimo è stato pubblicato poche ore fa, ma è quello pubblicato ieri, in cui si vede il personaggio controllato dal giocatore scrivere a suon di colpi di proiettili la scritta Leek su un muro, a confermare che il gruppo sembra essere effettivamente in possesso di una copia giocabile di GTA VI e non semplici video sottratti a Rockstar Games.

Sia come sia, tutti i video fin qui pubblicati hanno in comune dei watermark, che rimandano all'acquisto di una criptomoneta creata dal gruppo stesso. Cyberleek ha creato un proprio sito web sul quale nei giorni scorsi ha pubblicato una sorta di manifesto contro l'industria dei videogiochi, enunciando dei "comandamenti" che se violati da un'azienda la metteranno nel mirino del gruppo criminale: in sostanza gli hacker se la prendono con il sistema delle licenze digitali, i live service "ciucciasoldi" e i "finti DLC". " Se abbiamo potuto colpire Rockstar, nessuno è al sicuro " avvertono i cybercriminali, che chiedono le scuse da parte delle aziende di videogiochi che si sono macchiate di questi peccati.

I fondi raccolti tramite la criptomoneta servirebbero, secondo il gruppo, per lo sviluppo di un "progetto segreto" che dal tenore del manifesto servirebbe per colpire l'industria dei videogiochi. Nel frattempo in casa Rockstar ufficialmente tutto tace e non è stato emesso alcun comunicato. Oltre alla costante azione di rimuovere i video che vengono pubblicati sulle varie piattaforme di condivisione, Take-Two, la capogruppo di Rockstar, ha presentato un'ingiunzione per ottenere da Microsoft (per i servizi Xbox e OneDrive) e Discord tutti i dati che possono portare all'identificazione delle utenze connesse al gruppo Cyberleek.

La grande anteprima ufficiale di GTA VI intanto è programmata per il prossimo 27 agosto in streaming su Netflix.

items.title: Rosenberg: Shortage of petrol but not patriotism as Russians feel growing impact of war
items.summary: Drivers are waiting hours in fuel queues, as Moscow prepares to celebrate Russian Flag Day.
items.content:
At a petrol station in the south-east of Moscow, Svyatoslav has been queuing in his car for two hours.

The sign board up ahead has just been changed to show there's no fuel.

"They say there will be petrol here," Svyatoslav tells me optimistically. "They just don't know when. Maybe today, maybe tomorrow."

I ask him why he doesn't drive off and look for another place to fill up.

"I haven't got enough in the tank to do that," Svyatoslav replies.

Even if he had, there'd be no quick fuel fix for Svyatoslav. This week across Moscow, and in other parts of Russia, there have been long queues for petrol.

"Unscheduled repairs at oil refineries," explain Russian officials.

Those repairs have been triggered by Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil facilities. Such long-range attacks sparked major fuel shortages earlier this summer. The targeting of oil refineries has continued apace.

This time the queues in Moscow are even longer than before. The authorities appear to be struggling to resolve problems with refining capacity and logistics.

"The second wave of the fuel crisis is building," declared broadsheet Nezavisimaya Gazeta this week.

Driving around Moscow this week two things catch the eye: patriotic announcements on giant billboards about Russian Flag Day…and giant petrol queues.

Outside one Moscow petrol station I count 80 vehicles waiting in line.

"Last night I went to get petrol at 11pm," says Elizaveta who's queuing again for fuel. "By midnight I'd reached the front of the queue. Then they shut the petrol station until 2am."

"I drove into Moscow yesterday from the provinces," says Lyubov. "It was empty petrol stations all the way."

To stay calm in the queue Lyubov is stroking her pet dog Agatha.

"Everyone says there is a difficult situation in the country," Lyubov tells me. "Everyone connects this to that situation."

Before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 there were no drone attacks on Russian oil refineries - or on any facilities inside Russia. These strikes haven't forced the Kremlin to U-turn. It's continuing what it still calls the "special military operation", Russia's war on Ukraine.

That is extraordinary for a country widely recognised as an energy superpower and one of the world's leading exporters of crude oil.

To reduce the fuel shortage the government has also temporarily authorised the production and sale of lower-grade petrol, like Euro 2, which is faster to produce. Euro 2 contains up to 50 times more sulphur than modern Euro 5 and was banned in Russia in 2013.

"For modern cars," wrote the government newspaper Rossiyskaya Gazeta, "regular use of lower-grade petrol can increase the pressure on the fuel injector, spark plugs, oxygen sensors, the catalytic converter and soot filter. Euro 2 won't kill an engine on one re-fuelling. But it sharply reduces the margin of safety."

It's not just the targeting of oil facilities which have brought the war home to Russians.

Ukrainian strikes on distribution centres of Wildberries, Russia's equivalent of Amazon, are causing disruption to shoppers and economic pain for sellers.

This week President Vladimir Putin conceded that attacks on industrial facilities and infrastructure "do inflict damage; this is obvious. We understand this, we see it."

"There are no critical consequences from such attacks. There have not been and cannot be."

"It is a disconnect between people's feelings and the description of reality by Vladimir Putin, the description of his personal reality in his head," believes Andrei Kolesnikov, a columnist for independent news outlet Novaya Gazeta.

"Maybe he's trying to hypnotise himself that everything is okay."

Recent polling inside Russia, including by the Public Opinion Foundation, suggest that anxiety in society is rising. That would suggest that the Kremlin's message of 'keep calm and carry on' isn't landing.

"This permanent feeling of anxiety is with everyone right now. You feel that something is wrong. Anxiety is the main sentiment," says Kolesnikov.

"This regime doesn't demonstrate any model of the future: the nearest future, a middle- term future, a long-term future. We are 'great' right now. What are the qualities of this greatness? The petrol crisis? In that sense, the future is aborted. People are trying not to think about the future. The horizon of planning is very short."

A few minutes' drive from the petrol station where I'd been chatting with Svyatoslav, I spot another long queue.

The local authorities have set up stalls and put on a street concert to mark Russian Flag Day.

There may be a shortage of petrol. But not of patriotism. Not here.

"It's my country, my fate, my dream," croons a singer. "I'm raising my flag. The flag of my country."

Volunteers are handing out Russian tricolours to people on the square.

"Dear friends, we live in a wonderful country!" declares one of the speakers. "We know that we will always be victorious. I wish you peaceful skies, a good mood, comfort, prosperity and pride in our country."

Along with the candyfloss there are Kalashnikovs. At one stall children are being shown an array of military hardware, including hand-held rocket launchers. The kids are picking up the weapons and posing with them.

The patriotic presentation is lifting some people's spirits.

"Difficulties unite us," pensioner Tatyana tells me. "The harder things are, the stronger we get."

But the war is very much on people's minds - especially the Ukrainian drone attacks on the Moscow region.

"When you go to sleep you don't know if you'll wake up in the morning," Angelina tells me. "That's the only problem. Everything else is fine."

"The problems we have are high prices, petrol shortages and last night, for the first time, my windows shook…I heard 'boom boom!' another woman tells me.

"Right now, it's important to take care of your psychological state, so that it's strong and unbreakable. So that, whatever happens, you can say: 'Oh well, never mind.'

Comments like that suggest that Russians don't believe they can influence what's happening around them. All they feel they can do is try to adapt.

items.title: Google consentirà di personalizzare in modo preciso il proprio feed di Discover con un semplice prompt
items.summary: Si potranno definire in modo più accurato gli argomenti di interesse semplicemente spiegandolo con un prompt e Google personalizzerà di conseguenza le notizie selezionate in Discover all'interno dell'app Google e in Android ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Google ha annunciato una nuova funzione di personalizzazione di Discover, il feed di notizie accessibile dall'app Google e, su molti smartphone Android, direttamente dalla home screen. Cliccando sull'icona dei tre puntini per accedere alle funzioni avanzate su qualunque contenuto del feed di Discover, sarà ora possibile specificare liberamente con le proprie parole in un prompt come personalizzare ulteriormente la selezione degli argomenti o delle fonti di interesse da parte dell'algoritmo di Google.

Come mostrato nell'esempio, si interagisce sostanzialmente come con un chatbot: si scrive quello che si vuole ottenere, si ottiene una prima risposta e poi, proseguendo con la conversazione, si indirizza la personalizzazione verso un risultato sempre più vicino ai propri desiderata. Da quello che sembra il limite è solo la fantasia: si possono indicare direttamente le fonti cercate, così come usare criteri più generali. Un buon modo per andare a chiedere a Google di mostrarvi ancora più articoli di DDay.it nel vostro feed di Discover! Il roll out, spiega Google, è progressivo e la nuova modalità potrebbe non essere disponibile da subito per tutti.

items.title: Cerchi una videocamera di sicurezza? Questi modelli Arlo sono in offerta su Amazon
items.summary: Dalla sorveglianza degli esterni al controllo degli interni: le videocamere Arlo sono ora in offerta su Amazon ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Le telecamere WiFi Arlo sono pensate per chi vuole controllare casa in modo semplice e diretto. Ci sono diversi modelli in offerta, con funzioni smart e prezzi più convenienti. Ecco le proposte disponibili:

Questa telecamera Arlo è pensata per la sicurezza degli spazi esterni e funziona senza cavi. Registra in HD, integra un sensore di movimento e una sirena per segnalare eventuali intrusioni. La confezione include due telecamere bianche e un pannello solare, che permette di mantenerle cariche più a lungo senza doverle ricaricare spesso.

La videocamera Arlo Essential offre una buona autonomia, con una durata della batteria fino a quattro volte superiore rispetto ai modelli precedenti, così da ridurre la necessità di ricariche frequenti.

Registra video in 2K e offre una visione notturna a colori, permettendo di vedere con chiarezza ciò che accade anche in condizioni di scarsa illuminazione. La visuale di 130° e lo zoom 12x consentono inoltre di controllare meglio dettagli come volti, targhe e movimenti.

In caso di rilevamento di un movimento, i faretti e l'allarme integrati possono contribuire a scoraggiare eventuali intrusi. Grazie all'audio bidirezionale è possibile anche parlare con chi si trova davanti alla telecamera, salutare un visitatore o dare un avvertimento.

La videocamera Arlo Essential da 3 videocamere è ora su Amazon al prezzo scontato di 189,99 €.

Questa telecamera WiFi da esterno è dotata di un potente faro da 2000 lumen e offre una risoluzione video 2K HDR. Il design grandangolare a 160° e la visione notturna a colori garantiscono una copertura completa giorno e notte. Inoltre, è inclusa una sirena d'allarme per una sicurezza aggiuntiva.

items.title: Semi, il camion elettrico Tesla arriva in Europa
items.summary: Farà bella mostra di sé nel corso della fiera IAA di Hannover, dove saranno anche rivelati specifiche e dettagli ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Tesla porterà in Europa il suo camion elettrico Semi presentando specifiche e dettagli di lancio all’IAA Transportation di Hannover , dal 15 al 20 settembre. Il camion sarà esposto anche in fiera, ma per ora non si ancora nulla su autonomia europea, prezzi e data di vendita.

L’ annuncio è più concreto di quello del 2024, quando Tesla aveva mostrato il Semi alla stessa manifestazione senza però indicare un piano commerciale.

Negli States il camion è proposto in due versioni, la Standard Range, con autonomia dichiarata di 325 miglia (523 km), e la Long Range, capace secondo Tesla di 500 miglia (800 km). Entrambe usano tre motori, per una potenza complessiva dichiarata di 800 kW, e possono ricaricare fino a 1,2 MW con i sistemi Megacharger di Tesla.

I prezzi statunitensi sono di circa 260.000 dollari per la Standard Range e 290.000 dollari per la Long Range, con Tesla che ha avviato ad aprile la produzione sulla linea dedicata della Gigafactory Nevada, progettata secondo l’azienda per 50.000 mezzi l’anno.

Per quanto riguarda la sua diffusione a stelle e strisce, PepsiCo impiega quasi 100 Semi in California , mentre Einride ne ha ordinati 500 per la propria flotta in Nord America.

Einride è una società svedese di trasporto elettrico che opera anche negli Stati Uniti dal 2021. Il Nord America è oggi il suo secondo mercato, serve clienti come Amazon e gestisce corridoi merci in California, Texas, New Jersey, Illinois e Georgia. Le stesse rotte sulle quali saranno impiegati i Semi di Tesla.

Dalle nostre parti opera in Svezia, Norvegia e Germania e inoltre ha ottenuto permessi per la guida autonoma in quattro Paesi (Svezia, Norvegia, Belgio e Stati Uniti).

items.title: YouTube Premium aumenta il costo di tutti gli abbonamenti: fino a 4 euro in più al mese
items.summary: YouTube Premium aumenta in Italia il prezzo di tutti i piani: rincari tra 1 e 4 euro al mese, con il Family che sale a 29,99 euro. L’aumento medio è di circa il 15% ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
I primi ad accorgersi dell’ aumento di YouTube Premium sono stati gli utenti già iscritti al servizio, che hanno ricevuto una e-mail di questo tipo.

La data di fatturazione cambia ovviamente a seconda di quella della prima attivazione del piano, ma ciò che salta all’occhio, al di là dell’aumento, è la motivazione che sembra presa quasi tal quale da quella a cui siamo abituati da anni da parte delle compagnie telefoniche: “Questo aggiornamento ci consentirà di continuare a migliorare Premium e sostenere i creator e gli artisti che guardi su YouTube”.

I prezzi aggiornati e aumentati sono invece già validi per i nuovi utenti che da oggi si iscriveranno al servizio . YouTube Premium Individuale ha subito un aumento di 2 euro al mese, pari a 24 euro all’anno, mentre la sottoscrizione Famiglia cresce di 4 euro mensili per un totale di 48 euro in più annuali. L’aumento medio rispetto ai precedenti prezzi è di circa il 15%.

items.title: Bilibili, il "social ibrido" cinese per la GenZ è quasi pronto a conquistare il mondo
items.summary: Bilibili vuole uscire davvero dai confini cinesi. Nuova app internazionale, sito in inglese, e strumenti per creator. Ma non avrà gli stessi “problemi di sicurezza” di TikTok? ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Il nome Bilibili probabilmente non dirà molto alla maggior parte dei lettori occidentali, eppure si tratta di una delle piattaforme video più grandi della Cina, con oltre 376 milioni di utenti attivi mensili. È una via di mezzo tra YouTube , per la centralità dei creator e dei contenuti caricati dagli utenti, e servizi come Netflix o Twitch , dato che produce e distribuisce anche anime, serie, documentari e live streaming a pagamento.

Questa settimana la piattaforma ha rilanciato la versione internazionale della sua app (interrotta l’estate scorsa), disponibile su Android e con un prossimo arrivo su iOS.

Non è più richiesto un passaporto o un documento d'identità per registrarsi , condizione che in passato valeva anche per gli utenti che accedevano dall'estero al sito cinese, e l'app internazionale mescolerà contenuti globali e cinesi: un particolare importante che le consentirà di competere per il pubblico e i creator occidentali .

Secondo quanto riportato da Semafor , Bilibili sta assumendo community manager a Los Angeles, Londra, Città del Messico, San Paolo, Istanbul e Tokyo, ed è al lavoro per realizzare un sito in lingua inglese in modo da semplificare il caricamento dei video ai creator internazionali.

L'azienda starebbe inoltre sviluppando un sistema di moderazione dei contenuti basato su IA, con una sede dedicata a Singapore, e una piattaforma per collegare i creator ai marchi per contenuti sponsorizzati.

Proprio in considerazione di questa nuova apertura internazionale, potrebbero ritornare gli stessi interrogativi su censura, moderazione dei contenuti e sicurezza dei dati che negli Stati Uniti hanno portato TikTok a dover cedere le proprie attività americane a gennaio di quest’anno.

items.title: Galbot ET1 è il robot che copia i movimenti umani semplicemente guardando dei video
items.summary: Presentato alla World Robot Conference di Pechino con l'usuale spettacolare balletto, il robot sarebbe pilotato da un singolo modello di intelligenza artificiale capace di fare propri i movimenti degli esseri umani dopo averli osservati ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
La startup cinese di robot umanoidi Galbot ha presentato alla World Robot Conference in corso a Pechino il suo primo robot umanoide bipede, il primo dotato del nuovo modello di intelligenza artificiale AstraBrain, che secondo l'azienda consetirebbe al robot di imparare e imitare i movimenti degli umani semplicemente osservando dei video.

I video condivisi dall'evento di prestazione a Pechino mostrano il robot impegnato nell'ormai classica esibizione di danza, sfoggiando una naturalezza di movimento semplicemente sbalorditiva.

Secondo i resoconti dalla manifestazione, presso il proprio stand Galbot ha effettuato due dimostrazioni. Nella prima il robot ET1 ha eseguito un ballo dopo aver imparato i movimenti osservando un video di un ballerino professionista.

Nella seconda, Galbot ha semplicemente chiesto al robot di distribuire degli snack al pubblico, che avrebbe eseguito il comando improvvisando. Viene però fatto notare che non è stato possibile confermare l'autenticità delle demo, se cioè i movimenti fossero effettivamente spontanei o pre-programmati.

Secondo Galbot, il robot è pilotato da un solo modello di intelligenza artificiale in grado di occuparsi sia dell'interpretazione del mondo esterno, che del movimento dei componenti meccanici. A oggi però Galbot non ha rilasciato alcuna informazione riguardo alle specifiche tecniche del robot, alla data di uscita sul mercato e al prezzo.

items.title: Apple avrebbe licenziato decine di dipendenti che lavoravano al Vision Pro
items.summary: Apple avrebbe ridimensionato il gruppo che lavora al Vision Pro, mentre le priorità dell’azienda si spostano sulla nuova Siri e sugli smart glass attesi nei prossimi anni ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Apple avrebbe licenziato almeno 60 dipendenti legati gruppo di lavoro del Vision Pro . Lo ha riportato AppleInsider , citando una fonte che la testata ha definito attendibile.

Il gruppo non risulta comunque smantellato del tutto, ma il ridimensionamento confermerebbe una tendenza già emersa in passato, quando oltre un anno fa Mark Gurman di Bloomberg aveva raccontato la divisione del Vision Products Group, con Mike Rockwell spostato alla guida del rilancio di Siri.

Senza contare che a luglio Samsung Display ha deciso di chiudere il progetto di ricerca e sviluppo per il display in tecnologia micro OLED "on glass" che sarebbe stato destinato al Vision Pro economico.

I tagli arrivano inoltre dopo il rincaro del visore, salito a 3.699 dollari a giugno per l'aumento dei costi dei componenti di memoria, e dopo l'aggiornamento con chip M5 dello scorso ottobre.

Le priorità di Apple ora sono altre, cioè la nuova Siri e gli smart glass, la cui presentazione era ipotizzata per quest'anno con lancio all'inizio del 2027. Apple avrebbe però rivisto il calendario per riesaminare alcuni aspetti legati alla privacy, in un contesto segnato dalle critiche rivolte agli occhiali AI di Meta.

Il nuovo dispositivo punterebbe su fotocamere (con l’ipotesi anche di non registrare i video), Siri e Visual Intelligence, ma senza display AR.

items.title: Addio tegole solari di Tesla: le Solar Roof non erano economicamente sostenibili
items.summary: Le Solar Roof di Tesla escono di scena dopo quasi dieci anni senza avere mai sfondato. Non hanno mai raggiunto i volumi promessi da Musk ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Tesla ha smesso di produrre e fornire il Solar Roof, il tetto composto da tegole fotovoltaiche lanciato nel lontano 2016. Lo ha riportato Electrek, secondo cui l'azienda ha comunicato alla propria rete di installatori certificati che d’ora in avanti sarà disponibile solo la fornitura di pannelli solari tradizionali. Tesla avrebbe infatti concluso che le tegole solari non erano un prodotto economicamente sostenibile .

A riprova delle voci trapelate, sul sito dell'azienda la pagina tesla.com/solarroof reindirizza ora a tesla.com/solarpanels, e la voce "Solar Roof" è sparita dal menu Energy, che elenca solo pannelli solari, Powerwall e Megapack.

Il Solar Roof era stato presentato da Elon Musk a fine 2016 e venduto, solo negli USA, a partire dalla primavera del 2017 . Musk aveva promesso 1.000 installazioni a settimana entro la prima metà del 2020, ma secondo i dati di Wood Mackenzie il picco reale si è fermato tra le 21 e le 32 unità settimanali, per un totale stimato di circa 3.000 impianti installati negli Stati Uniti in 7 anni .

I prezzi, inizialmente indicati intorno ai 22 dollari a piede quadrato ( circa 237 dollari al metro quadro ), sono aumentati negli anni, in alcuni casi anche dopo la firma del contratto.

In ogni caso, Tesla aveva già smesso di comunicare i dati di installazione del Solar Roof nei bilanci trimestrali dall'inizio del 2024.

items.title: Tutto pronto per il lancio di Chang'e-7: sarà la prima missione a cercare ghiaccio al polo sud della Luna
items.summary: La missione cinese, che trasporta anche diversi strumenti scientifici internazionali, include anche un rover e un mini hopper, che esploreranno i crateri in ombra del polo sud della Luna per confermare la presenza di ghiaccio ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
La Cina si appresta a lanciare una delle missioni più ambiziose del suo programma lunare, Chang'e-7 . Il razzo Long March 5 con a bordo la sonda è sulla rampa di lancio del Wenchang Satellite Launch Center sull'isola di Hainan. In un comunicato, l'agenzia spaziale cinese spiega che i preparativi per il lancio stanno procedendo come da programma e la missione inizierà "presto". Gli alert di chiusura dello spazio aereo confermano però che la prima data di lancio utile sarà il 24 agosto, tra pochi giorni.

L'obiettivo di Chang'e-7 è la regione del polo sud della Luna , il luogo dove tutti i programmi spaziali puntano a riportare l'Uomo e gettare le basi per una presenza permanente. Il motivo è semplice: si ritiene infatti che nei crateri perennemente in ombra del polo sud ci sia la presenza di acqua in forma di ghiaccio , una risorsa inestimabile per le future basi sulla superficie della Luna. Ma nessuna missione ha fino ad ora esplorato la regione direttamente sulla superficie.

Chang'e-7 è tra le missioni più complesse fin qui tentate dal programma spaziale lunare cinese. La sonda è composta da quattro componenti: un orbiter, un lander, un rover e un "mini hopper" , un mezzo in grado di saltellare sulla superficie lunare per assistere il rover nell'esplorazione della regione e che integra strumenti per rilevare molecole d'acqua e isotopi di idrogeno. L'hopper, se tutto andrà bene, sarà in grado di prelevare e analizzare campioni di ghiaccio estratti dal sottosuolo fino ad una profondità di fino a circa 1 metro . L'interesse scientifico della missione è dunque elevatissimo.

Il sito scelto per l'allunaggio è il bordo illuminato del cratere Shackleton, esattamente in prossimità del polo sud geografico, il cui interno è perennemente in ombra. La missione porta con sé un totale di 21 strumenti scientifici, di cui 6 frutto di collaborazioni internazionali, incluso uno italiano, un riflettore Laser dell'Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare di Frascati.

La missione prevede che una volta raggiunta l'orbita lunare, Chang'e-7 trascorrerà diversi mesi a sorvolare e mappare dallo spazio l'area dell'allunaggio, prima di procedere con il distacco e la discesa del lander verso la superficie. La regione è particolarmente sfidante per compiere un allunaggio a causa della morfologia e dalle particolari condizioni di illuminazioni. Il requisito della missione è centrare il luogo dell'allunaggio con una precisione di 100 metri.
